The pivotal study in support of this NDA was Study 2005-01
A Historically-Controlled, Multi-Center Phase 3 Study to Determine Safety and Efficacy

Study 2005-01 was a multicenter, open-label, historical control study designed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of defibrotide for the treatment of hepatic VOD with evidence of multi-organ dysfunction following HSCT.

population.text: Adult and pediatric patients with severe hepatic VOD meeting Baltimore diagnostic criteria who also had multi-organ failure (pulmonary and/or renal dysfunction) following HSCT

citations.quote: those with severe VOD who met Baltimore diagnostic criteria for VOD (hyperbilirubinemia plus two of the following: ascites, \ge 5\% weight gain and hepatomegaly), who also had multi-organ failure(MOF,i.e., pulmonary and/or renal dysfunction, with or without CNS dysfunction)
## 2.2.4.1 Primary Endpoint - Survival at Day+100 Post HSCT

n.text: 102 patients in the defibrotide arm and 32 historical controls

citations.quote: The prospective historically controlled trial (Study 2005-01) enrolled 102 patients in the defibrotide arm and 32 historical controls.

result.text: Day +100 survival was 38% (95% CI: 29, 48) in the defibrotide arm vs 25% (95% CI: 12, 43) in the historical control arm

citations.quote: Efficacy results in Study 2005-01 evaluated by Day+100 survival after transplantation demonstrated an observed survival rate of 38% (95% CI: 29, 48) in the defibrotide arm compared to 25% (95% CI: 12, 43) in the historical control arm.

indication.text: Treatment of adult and pediatric patients with hepatic veno-occlusive disease (VOD), also known as sinusoidal obstruction syndrome (SOS), with renal or pulmonary dysfunction following hematopoietic stem-cell transplantation (HSCT)

citations.quote: DEFITELIO is indicated for the treatment of adult and pediatric patients with hepatic veno-occlusive disease (VOD), also known as sinusoidal obstruction syndrome (SOS), with renal or pulmonary dysfunction following hematopoietic stem-cell transplantation (HSCT).

target_moa.text: Mechanism not fully elucidated; defibrotide sodium enhances plasmin enzymatic activity to hydrolyze fibrin clots and, in vitro, increases t-PA and thrombomodulin and decreases vWF and PAI-1 expression, reducing endothelial cell activation and increasing EC-mediated fibrinolysis

citations.quote: The mechanism of action of defibrotide sodium has not been fully elucidated. *In vitro*, defibrotide sodium enhances the enzymatic activity of plasmin to hydrolyze fibrin clots.

defibrotide sodium increased tissue plasminogen activator (t-PA) and thrombomodulin expression, and decreased von Willebrand factor (vWF) and plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 (PAI-1) expression, thereby reducing EC activation and increasing EC-mediated fibrinolysis.

modality.text: Oligonucleotide (polydisperse mixture of predominately single-stranded polydeoxyribonucleotide sodium salts derived from porcine intestinal tissue)

citations.quote: Defibrotide sodium (DEFITELIO) is a polydisperse mixture of predominately single-stranded polydeoxyribonucleotide sodium salts derived from porcine intestinal tissue.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >=10%) were hypotension, diarrhea, vomiting, nausea and epistaxis; most common serious adverse reactions were hypotension (11%) and pulmonary alveolar hemorrhage (7%). Hypotension occurred in 65 (37%), diarrhea 43 (24%), vomiting 31 (18%), nausea 28 (16%), epistaxis 24 (14%) of 176 patients.

citations.quote: The safety of DEFITELIO was determined in 176 adult and pediatric patients with hepatic VOD with pulmonary and/or renal dysfunction following HSCT who were treated with DEFITELIO 6.25 mg/kg every 6 hours [see *Clinical Studies (14)*].

The most common adverse reactions (incidence \ge 10\% and independent of causality) were hypotension, diarrhea, vomiting, nausea, and epistaxis.
